What each one says it does

Quoted from each one's own pages, read October 27, 2026.

Google Hotels

"Hotel search on Google helps you discover, compare, and book accommodations for your trip." "Hotel prices come from Google partners like hotel owners, online travel agencies, metasearch engines, and other travel providers." "Hotels don’t pay Google to appear in hotel search results and can’t pay to influence their ranking." "If you click a booking link, you go to the partner website to complete your booking."

Google Travel Help, Search for hotels on Google, read October 27, 2026.

KAYAK

"KAYAK is a travel search engine, not a ticket seller." It says "we compare hundreds to thousands of travel sites in seconds". "Each provider sets its own prices, not KAYAK." "KAYAK doesn’t charge any extra fees." "Either way, the booking is with the provider, not with KAYAK."

KAYAK help, Search and discovery, read October 27, 2026.

trivago

"The trivago app is the easy way to search and compare hotel prices from your favorite booking sites"; "Compare accommodation prices from major booking sites with one search". Its app also offers price drop alerts: "Now you can sign up for price drop alerts on the trivago app to stay on top of price changes for your favorite hotels."

trivago on the App Store (seller trivago N.V.), read October 27, 2026. trivago.com, its help center and its company site answered our requests on October 27, 2026 with an error (HTTP 403), so the only trivago source here is its App Store listing.

The price checker and how Underbook works.

Measured, September 25 to October 10, 2026

KAYAK and trivago on Google Hotels itself

Google Hotels lists metasearch sellers beside the booking sites, among them KAYAK and a seller named "trivago DEALS". In our 16 price snapshots of September 25 to October 10, 2026 (6,620 hotel prices, a median of 12 sellers per hotel):

Sellers on Google Hotels in 16 snapshots, September 25 to October 10, 2026: how often each was listed, was the lowest, named a room and was priced before tax
Seller on Google HotelsListed atLowest of allNames a roomBefore tax
Booking.com90%41385%8%
Expedia68%23091%2%
KAYAK30%3130%37%
trivago DEALS33%2940%57%
The hotel's own site67%64553%19%
  • Like with like against Booking.com at 1,098 hotels, KAYAK was more than 2% lower at 227 of 1,098 (21%), Booking.com at 159 of 1,098 (14%), and the two were within 2% at 687 of 1,098 (63%).
  • Like with like against Booking.com at 1,052 hotels, trivago DEALS was more than 2% lower at 604 of 1,052 (57%) and Booking.com at 207 of 1,052 (20%). At 831 more hotels one of the two prices looked before tax and the other all-in (trivago DEALS' was the before-tax one at 811); those are left out.
  • Neither KAYAK's nor trivago DEALS' listings named a room or carried Google's free-cancellation label in these snapshots; Booking.com's named a room at 85%.

So the three overlap: Google Hotels itself lists KAYAK and trivago DEALS at many hotels. Whichever you open, the lower number is a lead: read its room and its total on the site that takes the booking.

Listed at: share of the 6,620 hotel prices where Google Hotels listed that seller. Lowest of all: hotel prices where its listing was the lowest of every site. Names a room: share of its listings that carried a room name. Before tax: share of its listings that sat near the before-tax going rate, at the hotels where taxes added 10% or more. Like with like: before tax against before tax and all-in against all-in. A price's basis is inferred from the hotel's two going rates (one nearer the before-tax going rate counts as before tax), only where taxes added 10% or more; a genuinely lower all-in price can sit there too, so the hotels where the two prices looked different are left out, not counted for either site. Hotels whose taxes added 2 to 10% are left out because no price's basis can be read there. Each snapshot: the lowest public price each booking site listed on Google Hotels for a US searcher, in US dollars, for a two-night stay, at one moment; not completed bookings, and not member or signed-in prices. A hotel priced in more than one snapshot counts once per snapshot. Method, charts and the per-hotel CSVs: the hotel price study.

What Underbook does differently

Underbook is built on the same list: for your hotel and dates it reads the booking sites Google Hotels lists (a median of 12 per hotel in our 16 price snapshots of September 25 to October 10, 2026). It does not search anywhere else. What it adds are three checks, with what they found in those snapshots (6,620 hotel prices):

Whether the lower price names the same room. At 4,783 of 6,620 (72%) hotel prices a listing was 5% or more below the going rate, typically 17% below. That listing named a room at 775 of 4,783 (16%), and named the same room as a listing at the going rate at 571 of 4,783 (12%). Underbook says which: "same room name", or that the lower listing needs a check before you book.

Taxes and fees as each site reports them. It shows each price all-in where the sites report taxes and fees (a resort or destination fee may be extra). That matters because sellers report differently: where taxes added 10% or more, KAYAK's listed price sat near the before-tax rate at 37% of hotels, Booking.com's at 8%.

The hotel's own site beside Booking.com. Google Hotels listed the hotel's own site at 4,425 of 6,620 (67%) hotel prices. Like with like against Booking.com, the hotel's site was more than 2% lower at 26% of 3,345 hotels and Booking.com at 13%; within 2% at 61%.

How to use them together

  1. Search your hotel and dates on one of them, Google Hotels, KAYAK or trivago.
  2. Note the hotel's own site if it is listed, and the lowest price with its site.
  3. Open the lower listing and read its room name and cancellation terms.
  4. Compare totals with taxes and fees on the last screen of each site, for the same room.

KAYAK, trivago and Google Hotels: common questions

Which is better for hotel prices, KAYAK, trivago or Google Hotels?+

None is lower every time; each lists many booking sites for one hotel and dates and sends you to the site you pick to book. Google Hotels says hotels cannot pay to influence their ranking, and in our 16 snapshots of September 25 to October 10, 2026 it listed the hotel's own site at 67% of hotel prices. Whichever you use, compare the total and the room on the booking site.

Does Google Hotels show KAYAK and trivago prices?+

Often. In our snapshots Google Hotels listed KAYAK at 30% of hotel prices and a seller named trivago DEALS at 33%, beside the booking sites.

Do I book on Google Hotels, KAYAK or trivago?+

Usually not on the tool itself. Google says that if you click a booking link you go to the partner website to complete your booking, and KAYAK says the booking is with the provider, not with KAYAK. trivago's app listing describes comparing prices from booking sites.

Why is the price different when I click through?+

A price can change between the search and the booking site, and some sellers list a price before tax. KAYAK says a price you see may no longer be available by the time you click through. Read the total on the last screen before you pay.

Is there a tool that checks whether the lower price is the same room?+

Underbook does, for the sites Google Hotels lists: for your hotel and dates it says whether a lower listing names the same room as one at the going rate. In our snapshots such a match was found at 571 of 4,783 hotel prices with a listing 5% or more below the going rate.
